title: First come, first kept
prompt:
A guest list has some names written down twice. Keep only the **first** time each name appears and drop every later copy, without changing the order of the names that stay.

Write `keepFirst(names)` that takes an array of 0 to 30 strings (each 1 to 3 lowercase letters) and returns a new array with every repeated string removed except its first appearance. Two strings are the same only if they are exactly equal. The input array must not be changed.

Examples:

- `keepFirst(["bo","al","bo","cy","al"])` returns `["bo","al","cy"]`
- `keepFirst(["x","y"])` returns `["x","y"]`
hints: As you walk through the list, what do you need to remember about the names you have already met?
Which tool can answer "have I seen this one before?" quickly, without scanning the whole result each time?
When you meet a name for the second time, should you add it to the result, and should it change what you remember?
